text:
rachel: Customer reports Go client hanging on streamed responses after adopting SDK v0.26.1. Happens ~1-2x/day, starts after ~30s into stream.

derek: Any error logs or stack traces?

rachel: No crash, goroutines pile up. Logs show: 
```
read loop: scan returned 0 bytes, no err
blocking on bufio.Scanner.Scan() forever
caller=stream.go:132
```

alex: Which model and response size? Is the server sending chunked JSON fragments or multiline JSON?

rachel: Model: gpt-neo-xt-3b (hosted). Payload is JSONL with nested objects and occasional arrays. We see truncated JSON objects at chunk boundaries. Customer downgraded server model code? they said no. Only change was they bumped SDK from v0.25.7 -> v0.26.1.

jordan: That SDK change touched the streaming scanner behavior (we switched to bufio.NewScanner with default token size). Could be a token too large or zero-len chunk handling change.

derek: Repro steps requested. Can you paste minimal repro client and server payload?

rachel: Pasted client repro below (sanitized):
```
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
req := redwood.StreamRequest{Model: "gpt-neo-xt-3b", Input: prompt}
resp, err := client.Stream(ctx, req)
for resp.Scanner.Scan() {
    chunk := resp.Scanner.Text()
    // decode json chunk
}
if err := resp.Scanner.Err(); err != nil { log.Println("scan err", err) }
```
Server sends chunked response like: `{"id":1,"text":"hello"}\n{"id":2,"text":"par`, then next chunk: `tial","meta":{...}}\n`

alex: That partial boundary shouldn't deadlock. bufio.Scanner returns false when token too long or on EOF. But "scan returned 0 bytes, no err" suggests it hit a zero-length read from the underlying reader and stayed blocked. Could be connection keepalive/flush semantics.

jordan: Two hypotheses: (1) SDK change removed a protective `ReadBytes('\n')` fallback so truncated tokens stall; (2) some proxies coalesce zero-len chunk frames for chunked transfer encoding.

rachel: Customer tried enabling retries/timeout but it just leaks goroutines. They see ~50 goroutines per hanging session.

derek: Ask customer for tcpdump? In the meantime, try reproducing with a local tiny server that sends exact chunk boundaries. I can run a quick go server to mimic.

support-bot: Created INC-4321, linked to customer acct acme-corp, priority P2. Assigned to eng-runtime. :spiral_note_pad:

alex: Quick mitigation: pin SDK to v0.25.7 for now. Also try setting a custom SplitFunc for scanner that tolerates partial JSON across tokens. Example fallback: use bufio.Reader.ReadBytes('\n') instead of Scanner.

jordan: I'll add an integration test that simulates zero-len chunk + fragmented JSON. Rachel, can you collect a short tcp-level capture and the exact SDK version + go runtime (go1.20/1.21)?

rachel: Will do and ping back. For repro we attached a tiny server snippet the customer ran:
```
ln, _ := net.Listen("tcp", ":8080")
for {
  conn, _ := ln.Accept()
  go func(c net.Conn){
    fmt.Fprint(c, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\n\r\n")
    fmt.Fprintf(c, "4\r\n%s\r\n", "{\"id\":1,\"text\":\"hi\"}\n")
    // send zero-length chunk accidentally
    fmt.Fprint(c, "0\r\n\r\n")
    time.Sleep(10*time.Second)
    fmt.Fprintf(c, "6\r\n%v\r\n", "{\"id\":2}\n")
    c.Close()
  }(conn)
}
```
alex: That 0 chunk in the middle explains it — chunked transfer `0\r\n\r\n` signals end-of-stream. If a proxy rewrites things or a bug sends it early, client will wait for more that never comes. Previously we may have treated spurious 0-length differently.

derek: Action items: (1) eng-runtime to reproduce and add unit test (jordan), (2) support to ask customer for pcap and go runtime (rachel), (3) recommend immediate pin to v0.25.7 and a server-side patch to avoid premature zero chunk.

jordan: I'll open a PR with tests + a fallback to `ReadBytes('\n')` if Scanner behaves unexpectedly. Marking as blocking for next patch release.

rachel: Thanks all, I'll update INC-4321 with tcpdump soon. :thumbsup:
